title: Wild Smoked Canadian Salmon Noodles
description: A quick and nutritious Canadian dish featuring wild smoked salmon, dark soy sauce, and earthy flavors, perfect for a weeknight dinner. This recipe incorporates an ice-bath shock to stop cooking and preserve the salmon's texture.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the soba noodles according to package instructions.
Prepare an ice bath by filling a large bowl with ice and water.
Once the noodles are cooked, immediately plunge them into the ice bath to stop cooking and preserve texture.
Cut the wild smoked Canadian salmon into thin slices and set aside.
Heat the sesame oil in a large skillet over medium heat and add the grated ginger, cooking for 1 minute.
Add the sliced green onions to the skillet and cook for an additional 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the cooked noodles to the skillet, tossing to combine with the ginger and green onion mixture.
Add the dark soy sauce to the skillet and toss to combine, cooking for an additional 1-2 minutes.
Divide the noodle mixture among plates and top with sliced wild smoked Canadian salmon.
Season with salt and black pepper to taste, garnishing with chopped fresh cilantro if desired.
Refrigerate and consume within 1 week — this preparation is not shelf-stable without an approved acid level and canning process.

Refrigerator pickle only: store in the fridge and consume within 1 week. For shelf-stable canning, add at least 2 tablespoons of vinegar (5% acidity) per cup of brine and follow a tested water-bath process.
